messages:
maria: FYI prod just hit a KV cache OOM during a long multi-doc generation. Observed around 3470012345. Not the usual slab thrash — looks like allocator hit a large contiguous request from the radix allocator when sequence length jumped.
josh: Ugh. Any repro payloads or trace IDs? Is this the kernel selection path that recently landed the async-kernel fallback? :thinking:
maria: Trace ids: trace=tx-9f2c; request examples attached (pasted below). Sequence length spikes to ~120k tokens due to recursive summarization in the user flow. We saw a sudden 100% KV alloc attempt for ~1.2GB chunk, allocator refused -> OOM.
tala: Can you paste the kv_stats dump? Also what batching mode was in use (adaptive vs greedy)?
maria: kv_stats from the host:
```
kv_total_capacity: 32GB
kv_used: 31.1GB
kv_frag_pct: 12.3
kv_active_sessions: 142
kv_longctx_sessions(>50k): 7
allocator_radix_peak: 1.2GB
evict_attempts: 3
spillback_count: 0
```
josh: Interesting — spillback_count=0. The spillback code path is supposed to trigger before hard failure. Possible ordering bug when radix allocator requests contiguous run crossing slab boundaries. If it can't split it down, it fails instead of trying fallback split path.
ryan: Also check kernel selection log: when seq len grows we switch kernels for attention; that can increase transient KV allocation due to different cache line sizes + KV copy. If switching and batching happen together you can get aligned large allocations.
maria: We have a short log snippet where kernel switch and a batching resize coincide:
```
[11:47:02] kernel_select: longseq_kernel (switch)
[11:47:02] batch_manager: grow_batch_count from 8 -> 24
[11:47:03] kv_alloc: requesting radix=1.2GB contiguous
[11:47:03] kv_alloc: failed -> oom
```
tala: Repro plan: run the failing request in a local canary with instrumentation: set BATCHER_MODE=adaptive and FORCE_KERNEL=longseq, enable KV_FAIL_FAST=off to observe fallback. We should also run heap profiling to see fragmentation map.
josh: Quick mitigation suggestions:
- short-term: enable small-batch cap for longctx sessions (cap batch size to 8) to avoid growth spikes
- mid-term: improve radix allocator fallback to allow splitting large contiguous requests into smaller chunks with temporary redirection to spillback pool
- immediate emergency: route longctx traffic to dedicated pool (rdw-dedicated-longctx) which has higher KV headroom
maria: Can we do an emergency canary? deploy-bot: deploy triggered by maria: canary/longctx-cap (1%) -> started 3470012358 :rocket:
ryan: Also propose a graceful degradation mode: mark sessions that exceed 30k tokens as 'stream-minimal' — reduce batching, enable KV prefix-only caching (only keep last N steps), and if allocation still fails, fallback to quantized smaller model (gptq-8bit) or route to a lower-cost replica that prefers low memory profile.
tala: For the allocator fix: implement a "split-allocate-then-link" path: if contiguous request > slab_size and failed, allocate multiple slab-sized buffers and present them as a virtual contiguous KV via scatter-gather. That avoids copy-heavy spillback but needs KV lookup indirection (fast in our runtime). Adds ~3% per-token cost but prevents OOM.
josh: Perf regression root cause hypothesis: kernel switch + aggressive adaptive batching allowed batch count to triple within 100ms which produced a burst of KV allocations. We should gate batch growth on available KV headroom (kv_used < kv_capacity - hysteresis). Add a batch_growth_check that consults an async kv_headroom signal.
maria: Agreed. For rollout plan I propose:
1) immediate 1% canary: enforce longctx batch cap + route new longctx sessions to dedicated pool (canary started)
2) 24h telemetry: track kv_alloc_failures, spillback_count, avg_fragmentation, per-session token histogram
3) deploy allocator fallback (split-alloc) in staging with unit tests
4) kernel/batcher coordination change: add kv_headroom check before growth; rollout to 10% then 50%
5) longer-term: implement virtualized scatter-gather KV and opt-in prefix-only cache policy
ryan: I can own the headroom metric + batch_growth_check. Will prototype a lightweight shared-memory kv_headroom beacon.
tala: I'll take the allocator split-alloc POC and perf test it.
josh: I'll add a smoke test in our replay harness that simulates 100 concurrent longctx sessions with synthetic recursion to ensure no hard OOMs and acceptable perf overhead.
maria: Thanks. I'll keep the canary running and post updates. If anyone sees more failures ping in this thread. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary/longctx-cap deployment finished on 1% hosts at 3470012362 :white_check_mark:
maria: initial canary telemetry: kv_alloc_failures dropped to 0 on canary hosts; batch growth stayed under cap; latency tail increased +1.8% for those sessions — acceptable for now.
ryan: good signal. We'll proceed with allocator POC and headroom check.
josh: adding an alert to incidents if kv_alloc_failures > 3 across 5min window for non-canary hosts.
maria: copied. closing loop here, will update once split-alloc POC passes perf tests.
